I'm fairly new to Star Trek, and while I plan on watching every series eventually, I'm curious what everyone liked the best. Also, if you have any order in which you recommend watching the series for a first-timer, I would be really interested.
What's your favorite series and why?

I'll start with my first impressions, I guess.

I started with TOS and couldn't get into it for some reason, but I had better luck with TNG and Voyager. I'm guilty of having Netflix on in the background while doing other things, though, so I'm likely to rewatch both series with my full attention at some point.
Favorite? I'd have to say "Enterprise" - I like how it tries to fill in a lot of back-story for the rest of the Star Trek universe, and how they had to learn new things as they went.

I loved how they explained why Klingons had humanoid foreheads in the TOS and the normal ruffled one on ENT and every other installment. Something that was refrence on a TNG episode when they where sent back to the TOS enterprise and worf remarked something along the lines of "klingons would rather not speak of this".

DS9 for the fact that it got away from the unbelievable version of humanity Roddenberry created. It dived into each race and developed the characters of each. It wasn't afraid to blow shit up. Dominion war was epic. And I loved most of the characters in DS9 which I can't really say for any other series.

We had to endure characters like Torres, Janeway, Picard, Trois, Crusher, Crusher, Riker, Kim etc... But with DS9 we got the best of TNG with O'Brien and Worf and we got awesome characters like Quark, Odo, Rom, Jadzia, Bashir, Garak, Dukat...

The acting was great, the dialogs were great, the monologues were great and the battles were better than the movies.

My favorite is TOS. When I was a kid, private TV stations were pretty new (in Germany) and they bought a lot of old stuff because its cheaper than buying the latest hit show. I was allowed to watch the daily TOS episode before I had to go to bed. Therefore TOS will always be my favorite show. A lot of the topics are still quite actual, despite the fact that TOS is almost 50 years old.
The Next Generation , because it was my first. :)

I grew up watching TNG, so that one is going to always hold a special place in my heart.

I know this next statement is going to be blasphemous to some, but Voyager was my favorite. The whole theme of solitude. Every other series had some form of support from Starfleet. I know that it starts off a bit slow. The first season is a bit tough to get through, but the series really does get better as it goes. I also know that this is my opinion and its not the most popular opinion. But what can I say, I like what I like.

I think I am skewed. I know this is a late response but I am going to bite anyways.

I am about halfway through TOS at the moment after watching TNG. I've been slowly watching it rather than binge watching in order to keep a steady pace. I barreled through TNG and feel like I would have had a better understanding had I taken my time.

So with that being said, I think TOS is my favorite series at the moment. It was very hard to get into and the majority of the characters show their age from being developed in a different era. I still pick up on religious references and sometimes the costumes are hard to ignore. Other than that, I think that each character has its pros and cons as well as each episode.

I'll detail my top three characters in TOS -

Kirk - Great captain that loves his crew and his ship. Doesn't back down from a fight but often makes foolish decisions based on emotion. On the flip side, some of his decisions are absolutely brilliant and get them to safety in the nick of time. All in all, amazing captain that might fit better on a fighter ship rather than the enterprise on an exploration mission. Would not make it during the TNG era with the prime directive.

Spock - Amazing character all around. I can find no cons with Mr. Spock as that would be most illogical.

McCoy - This is a love hate relationship. I think I like him so much because I can't stand him most of the time. If that makes any sense. He's obviously an amazing doctor and surgeon and I often yell at the TV when he tries to comment on mission plans or in the middle of a tense situation. "Save the people Jim, they want to be saved from this cultural loop that they have been in for generations!" SHUT UP LEONARD! /rant Other than that, he makes me smile often due to his quirky attitude as well as telling Kirk exactly what is on his mind. The great thing about being the ship doctor is that he can speak his mind.

all in all, I am sure I'll go back to loving TNG just as much when I watch through it again. I am just in love with TOS for now.

The two overlook the settlement.

"Look Mamoru, dinner for the night" says Akane.

Down below in the village, the citizens are closing up shops, putting away the horses, and preparing to put down for the night. Guards are at each of the trail entrances into the town, but no wall is put up. The guards acknowledge several people leaving. This town is a perfect target for Akane and Mamoru. They can enter and exit without being seen.

"This reminds me of home" Akane mentions. Mamoru, ever silent, doesn't respond. Even though the two share a cerebral connection, Akane still likes to talk verbally. It is lonely on the road. Akane plans the attack.

The trail entrances are on either end of the village, and no guards on the perimeter. That is where they will enter. What appears to be a tavern is close to the east end, away from the river. No, a 4 foot tall dog (standing on all fours) would certainly stand out.

Maybe the beggars? No one would care if they went missing, but in the past Akane felt that they have little flavor. Wait, the river! There might be fishermen down by the river they could feast upon. Akane makes it official.

"Mamoru, we will att-" Akane is interrupted.

"Who are you!" A large tall man demands an answer. He is followed closely by 3 of his men, all four of which are armed. One of them raises his rifle, centering it on Akane. Before she can talk her way out of this, Mamoru leaps into action. He attacks the man aiming the rifle at Akane, taking him down.

"NO! STOP!" But it was too late. Mamoru killed the hunter, and the other three pulled out their weapons, took aim, and put Mamoru down.

Akane is furious, whispering a spell to herself, her face turns read, her hands glow, and in an instant a red flash appears! If those in the village would be looking out their window, a great red light would appear on the hill above.

What is left, is little. Mamoru's corpse had disintegrated. The hutners were transformed into a pile of ash, and Akane, there was nothing left of her.

Very interesting. It seems like there is a fascinating dynamic between Akane and Mamoru, something that I'd like to explore even further.

Thank you for writing this :)

The little you've written suggests a fascinating story. Why are the two planning an attack on the village? What formed this cerebral bond? Is theirs a world infused with both technology and magic? The character names and descriptions are solid as well.

The small timeframe in which this occurs makes it difficult to relate to any of the characters or get a grasp of what's happening before all of the involved characters vanish in a flash of magic. Great potential, though!

Snow crunches under her boots as Kryvaal the huntress makes her way through the frozen wasteland of winter. Creaking and groaning under the weight of the wailing and shrieking snow filed winds as they whip past. Her hound a Sloa Ahk faithfully follows her every move, carefully treading as if to tip toe its lumbering hulk of a body around the landscape.

As the wind fades ever so slightly the hounds ears perk up and its nose frantically grasps at the frosty air for scent with a fierce cloud of condensation pillowing out of its nostrils as it exhales.

“What is it Cheahak? Slow. Lead me.” she commands the beast, in a tacit almost curt but gentle order.

Creeping slowly the hound winds its way through the trees as they sing their song of groans and creaks, the whistle a melody in the branches. Winding into a dense and thick forest the the sounds grow only louder when suddenly a branch breaks loose with a thundering crack that splits the drone and itself from the tree. Taking others with it on its way down with more snaps and cracks the cacophony finally ceases.

Cheahak undaunted by the events continues along when finally a small clearing with a single bush of berries emerges from the snow. Green beacon shining in the white and brown wasteland a small Aariz a deer like animal grazes on the leaves and berries. With a low and nearly silent growl the hound almost asks for the next command expectantly looking to his master.

“wait, this one is my turn” she says, nocking an arrow into her bow gently and drawing steadily back. “you may kill the next” she says in a hushed whisper as she begins to hold her breath to steady her aim.

Faster than can be seen the arrow is propelled expertly into the neck, severing not only the brainstem but the main arteries to it. Falling lifeless before it could process what happened the aariz collapses dead to the ground. Duo of huntress and hound making their way now more openly towards their quarry.

“will feed us for days Cheahak, days.” she assures the hound who now looks angry and betrayed, her words only met with a snarl of dissatisfaction. “I sad you get the next kill, quiet now. We eat soon.” reassuring the beast the words seem to bring it comfort.

He calms down and sits next to his master watching her break down the quarry helping where he can. The pair working in harmony, as always.
